claims.text: WxTaTiVCr alloys with 32–90 at.% W can be fabricated by powder metallurgy and spark plasma sintering with in-situ TiC formation.
The resulting alloys have a BCC crystal structure and a multiphase microstructure.
The alloys contain a well-dispersed population of nanoscale TiC precipitates.
Alloying elements in the BCC matrix produce lattice strain or distortion and solid-solution strengthening.
Lattice distortions impede dislocation motion.
TiC produces dispersion strengthening and contributes to improved hardness and strength in WxTaTiVCr-derived alloys.
TiC precipitates pin dislocations.
TiC precipitates pin and stabilize grain boundaries.
Combined solid-solution and TiC dispersion strengthening govern high-temperature plastic strain and toughness.
The combined mechanisms increase high-temperature yield strength while retaining enough plasticity to maintain toughness.
At 600–1000 °C, TiC-containing samples should have higher yield strength than compositionally identical samples in which TiC is suppressed.
At 600–1000 °C, TiC-containing samples should have greater plastic strain capacity than samples in which TiC is suppressed.
At 600–1000 °C, TiC-containing samples should have improved fracture toughness relative to samples in which TiC is suppressed.
An optimal TiC-containing alloy could show a twofold or greater improvement in toughness metrics over the baseline.
A comparison between TiC-promoting and TiC-suppressing processing at otherwise identical composition and test conditions would isolate the effect of TiC.
C15 Laves phases occur when W content exceeds approximately 70 at.%, creating a possible secondary-phase complication within the proposed range.
The mechanism is expected to hold across approximately 32–90 at.% W and 600–1000 °C.
The mechanism may not apply to non-refractory alloys or systems dominated by other strengthening mechanisms.
The relative quantitative contributions of solid-solution and dispersion strengthening have not been established.

Failure to observe a statistically significant reduction in high-temperature plastic strain and toughness after TiC suppression would falsify the claim that TiC dispersion strengthening is a key governing factor.

contradictions.description: The groups are required to have identical overall compositions, but minimizing carbon to suppress TiC changes the carbon content and therefore the overall composition unless carbon is explicitly treated as an uncontrolled processing impurity.
The intervention calls for identical elemental ratios, whereas the baseline alternatively permits higher W content. Changing W content confounds the intended isolation of TiC precipitation.
